reconcile.note: Gill distinguishes pleasing that seeks others' good and edification, as in Romans 15:2, from flattery that hides or corrupts the gospel, which Galatians 1:10 condemns.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible pairs Paul's boast in 1 Corinthians 10:33 that he pleases all men against his flat denial in Galatians 1:10 as a Yes/No contradiction.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.
sides.verseText: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.

sides.snippet: For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn't be a servant of Christ.
sides.verseText: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn't be a servant of Christ.
